answers.confusing_rules: None were materially ambiguous during this game. The visit rules are dense, though: it is easy to confuse whom a Tracker targets with who visited that target, or to overlook that a hidden Sleepwalker trait can add another visit.
answers.missing_information: No essential information was missing for my own choices. Hidden roles and traits did make some public claims hard to verify, as intended. My Night 2 Tracker result (Erin visited nobody) was not included in my last will, which still said the result was pending.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to update my last will with my Night 2 result after receiving it, but I died before I had a chance to edit it during the Day. I understand the rule against adding night results to a will that same night, but the result being available to me while the will stayed stale was awkward.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None found. Alice's identification of Grace as the visitor she killed was an inference from her Veteran report and the announced cause of Grace's death; Dave's watch showed Grace visited Erin, not that Erin was her only destination. Grace's hidden Sleepwalker trait explains the additional visit.
answers.suggestions: Consider an explicit notice that a will is frozen for the night and will not include results received that night, especially if its owner dies before the next Day. A structured night summary distinguishing visits, astral actions, and additional trait visits could also make visit-based claims easier to assess without revealing hidden information.

answers.confusing_rules: The rules are extensive, and the interactions between ordinary actions, automatic trait actions, visits, and role-blocks are easy to lose track of. In particular, it takes careful reading to see that Grace could visit Erin with her Pharmacist action and also visit Alice through Sleepwalker; Bob's claim that Alice's account required an additional visit was reasonable, but not a contradiction.
answers.missing_information: During play, I could not know other players' hidden traits or roles, so I could not tell whether Grace had an extra Sleepwalker visit or verify Alice's Veteran claim directly. That uncertainty is intentional, but a concise, persistent summary of publicly established visits and claims would make it easier to compare new claims against earlier results.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: As Lookout, I would have liked to watch both Erin and Alice on Night 2 to check the competing visit claims, but I could target only one player. This seems like an intentional role limitation rather than an interface problem.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None noticed. The apparent tension between Grace visiting Erin and Alice saying Grace visited her is consistent with Grace having the Sleepwalker trait and making an additional random visit.
answers.suggestions: Offer a compact, persistent evidence panel separating confirmed public facts, unverified claims, and private results. For visit evidence, show the destination and visitor while making clear that a Lookout result does not say the target was visited only by those players. A brief reminder that automatic trait actions can add visits would also help players assess claims without making hidden traits public.

answers.confusing_rules: No materially ambiguous rule stood out. One interaction that is easy to overlook is that a Sleepwalker makes an extra random visit in addition to any role action; since traits are private, a public visit report may not explain every visit.
answers.missing_information: As Sheriff, I could not distinguish a real role-block from the hidden Drowsy trait, which can also cause a block with no blocker. Deaths reveal causes but not roles, so several claims remained unverified until the game ended.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: No interface-specific action. In-game, I wanted to confirm whether Bob held the Katana and identify who blocked me, but my Sheriff results could not establish either.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: None that I can identify as a rules or program bug. Bob's no-kill Night 1 plan was unusual, but legal. His argument that Grace needed an unexplained second visit overlooked the possibility of a Sleepwalker trait; that was a player deduction error, not a mechanics inconsistency.
answers.suggestions: Consider a compact persistent summary of claims, results, deaths, and votes, plus a clearer indicator of whether a blocked action could also have been caused by a hidden trait. The Day 2 discussion repeated the same requests and conclusions many times; stronger incentives or interface prompts to share new information rather than restate positions could make long Days less repetitive.

answers.confusing_rules: Sleepwalker and swaps were hard to reason about from the public record. The Sleepwalker trait is hidden, so a Veteran's "one visitor" result could come from a random visit that no one can see. A Veteran alert reports only a count and whether the attack hit, so "that was Grace" is a deduction from the cause of death, not an observation. The rules say the alert result does not identify the visitor, but the claim format invites players to name one. Day 1's "at most 2 rounds" and the rule that a Day ends after a full round with no public message or nomination were not obvious from the speaking-order messages, so I had to infer when the Day would close.
answers.missing_information: I could not see a running tally of each player's remaining speaking budget or the carry-over amount at the start of each Day, so I could not judge how much I could afford to say before the round multipliers rose. I had no list of who held which trait, which is correct by design but made the Veteran and Sleepwalker reasoning guesswork. The trial vote split was public, but I could not see which players were Yakuza, so I could not confirm whether the Sheriff and Tracker checks were consistent with the Katana holder rule. A nomination tally that marks the nominator's automatic Yes would also have helped.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask a single player a question privately without it appearing in the public ledger as a private message; the ledger shows who PMed whom, which is a strong signal in itself. I also wanted to test a claim by asking the Veteran for the visitor's role, which the rules do not allow. As a Jester, I had no way to make the town trust a nomination without looking like bait, so a self-nomination was my only lever.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken in the mechanics I could check. Carol's death and her last will came out on Day 3, and the Veteran alert result on Night 2 matched the Sleepwalker visit that killed Grace. One oddity: Grace's Night 2 private result said "You visited Erin tonight" and did not mention her Sleepwalker visit to Alice, which is consistent with a hidden trait but made Alice's claim hard to check. Also, the game ended right after Bob's execution, which is correct, but the final message did not state which faction won or why, so I had to work it out.
answers.suggestions: Show a running speaking-budget line on each turn (current balance, carry-over, and the price of the next message) so players can plan. Add a short end-of-game summary stating which win condition ended the game. Consider a neutral public note when a hidden trait effect (Sleepwalker, Armed, Paranoid) fires, so visit-based claims can be checked more fairly. Show the nomination tally with the nominator's automatic Yes marked, and give each player a "whose vote counted" reminder after a trial so investigators can verify claims.

answers.confusing_rules: The Sleepwalker trait is the hardest part to reason about. Each night it visits a random living player, and the player is never told whom. That hidden visit is what made Alice's Veteran claim work on Night 2 (Grace's random visit landed on Alice), but nobody at the table could know it existed. Bob argued that Alice's "that was Grace" needed a second Grace visit that the public record doesn't show. He was right about the record, so the town had no way to resolve the question. The rules also don't say whether a Sleepwalker's random visit is visible to anyone beyond "counts as a visit".
answers.missing_information: As a dead Yakuza, I had no information after Night 2. I didn't know who my Sleepwalker visited on either night, and I had no way to see what the living players saw in the visit record. The Veteran's alert log doesn't say who visited, so Alice's claim could only be checked by reasoning about visit counts. A short per-player visit log for the living would have helped settle the Alice question on Day 3.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to coordinate a Day 3 plan with Bob, for example whether to defend him or vote Innocent to keep the Yakuza alive. We had only night chat, and his Day 3 PMs went to Frank and Heidi, not to me. I also wanted to know what my own trait had done, which the game deliberately hides. A private result showing my Sleepwalker's target would have made the trait less of a blind spot.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing I could confirm was broken. The night results were internally consistent: Alice's "1 visitor" matched my Sleepwalker visit to her, Dave's watch on Erin matched Carol's and my visits, and Erin's block matched my Pharmacist action. Carol's last will said "result pending" for her Night 2 track, which fit her death during the night.
answers.suggestions: Give every player with a hidden trait a private note of the trait's visit target or effect each night, since that is the only way they can judge the claims made about them. Also consider showing the Yakuza a short summary of the Katana holder's Day PMs, since PMs between teammates are visible events and tend to drive the town's reads.

answers.confusing_rules: Trait visits were hard to reason about. A Sleepwalker's random visit counts for Veteran alerts and Trackers, but nobody is told the trait exists. Grace's Sleepwalker visit to Alice on Night 2 is what made Alice's "that was Grace" account possible, yet from the public record it looked impossible. The rules are clear once written down, but a player can't check them from the public record. A Veteran's alert kill tells you a visitor died, not who, so the claim depends on knowing about hidden visits.
answers.missing_information: I couldn't track the Day-by-Day speaking budget or the price table from this transcript, so I couldn't judge whether long messages were affordable. I also had no running record of each player's past votes beyond the ledger. The ledger's private-message line shows only that a PM happened, not its contents, so it was hard to weigh Bob's PMs to Grace and to Frank/Heidi against the rest of the evidence.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to ask Alice a private question about how Grace reached her without making the question public. A PM is visible as an event, so any private question became a public signal. I also wanted a way to test Veteran-visit claims against possible hidden Sleepwalkers without revealing anything. I had no tool for that.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing clearly broken. Two oddities: (1) Carol's last will says "Night 2: tracking Erin; result pending", and her Tracker result on Erin was "visited nobody". That is consistent, since Erin was blocked, but the public record doesn't show the block, so it reads as a contradiction. (2) Alice's and Grace's Sleepwalker visits produced visits no public record showed. That's by design, but it makes the visit logs look inconsistent to anyone who doesn't know about the trait.
answers.suggestions: Consider a rules note that hidden-trait visits are never corroborated publicly. Surface the speaking budget and price table in the ledger so players can plan. Let the Veteran's alert result say "a visitor died" rather than "your attack killed them", since the current wording reads as an identity claim. Keep showing each player's last will in full at death, as it did here.

answers.confusing_rules: 1) What Yakuza know about each other's roles. R2/R8 say Yakuza "know each other" but don't say whether they know their teammates' roles. On Night 1 Bob wrote "Grace, if you hold a Pharmacist block", as if he wasn't sure. Yet the end-of-night Yakuza summary names roles ("Grace (Pharmacist)"). I had to decide whether that leak was intended. 2) What goes in the Yakuza night summary when a teammate has a trait. I left Grace's Sleepwalker visit out because traits are hidden even from teammates (R24). R8 says "each Yakuza learns what actions the other Yakuza chose", though, so it's unclear whether chosen trait actions like Spare Blade should be listed. 3) What a Pharmacist is told about her own block. R9 only says a blocker learns whether the block failed because the target can't be blocked. No result message is defined for a block that worked, so I told Grace "You visited Erin tonight". That is not a real result type. 4) R16 explains how the Day ends but not how to report the reason. Day 2 ended with a generic "Discussion time is over", and players can't tell whether it hit the 8-round cap or a quiet round.
answers.missing_information: 1) I had no single resolution table showing, for each night, every visit in one place: role actions, Sleepwalker visits and the Katana. I had to rebuild it by hand to check the Lookout, Tracker and Veteran results. On Night 2 that meant Grace→Erin (block), Grace→Alice (sleepwalk), Alice→Carol (sleepwalk), Bob→Carol (Katana) and Carol→Erin. Erin's visit to Grace was removed because she was blocked. 2) I had no running count of each player's speaking budget or round number, so I couldn't confirm when Day 2 hit its round cap. 3) I had no automatic win check showing which living players block wins. After Bob was hanged I had to confirm by hand that Frank, the Jester, doesn't block wins, so the Village won with Frank still alive.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: 1) Send Grace a proper "your block was applied" or "no feedback" message instead of the improvised "You visited Erin tonight". 2) Attach a short reason when a Day ends (round cap or quiet round). 3) Mark trait-driven visits in my own log as automatic, so a review can separate them from chosen actions.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Nothing I found broke the rules. I checked every result against the hidden actions. Night 1: Carol's "Bob visited no one" and Dave's "nobody visited Grace" were both correct; Alice's sleepwalk visit went to Bob and Grace's to Heidi. Erin's Not Evil on Bob was correct because he held the Katana. Night 2: Grace's random sleepwalk hit Alice, who was on alert, so the Veteran killed her. Dave's Lookout correctly showed Carol and Grace visiting Erin. Carol's Tracker correctly showed Erin visiting nobody, because Erin was blocked. The win check was correct: after Bob's hanging the only Yakuza were dead, the Jester doesn't block wins, and the Village won while Frank lost. Oddities: 1) Grace's improvised result line (see above). 2) Two players got the same Sleepwalker trait in an 8-player game. That's legal, but it produced a visit (Grace→Alice) that no player could explain, and the Day 3 trial turned on it. Bob argued correctly that the visit record didn't fit Alice's Veteran claim. 3) Dave spoke first on both Day 1 and Day 2. That's a legitimate random result, but it can look like the order isn't random.
answers.suggestions: 1) Define standard result messages for blockers and other roles with no stated feedback, so moderators don't improvise. 2) State plainly in R8 whether Yakuza learn their teammates' roles at the start. 3) Give the moderator a per-night visit graph that includes automatic and trait visits, and have it pre-compute the Lookout, Tracker and Veteran results. 4) Include the reason in the Day-end announcement. 5) Consider limiting visit-adding traits like Sleepwalker to one per small game, or at least note in R24 that duplicates are possible. 6) Give the moderator an automatic win-check display that lists the living players who block wins.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went

task:
If you played this game again, what tips and tricks do you wish you'd known? Give 1-5 concrete, reusable lessons (not a recap of this game), each with a topic and who it applies to (a role, a faction, or 'everyone').

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: Before calling a visit claim a lie, check hidden traits. A Sleepwalker visits a random player each night and nobody is told. Grace's Sleepwalker visit on Alice explained Alice's Veteran kill, and the town wrongly treated it as impossible. Ask whether any living or dead player could have had such a trait before voting Guilty on a 'the visits don't fit' argument.

When an argument against a claimant depends on a public visit log, list the hidden sources that could add a visit: Sleepwalker, Katana holder, Yakuza Spare Blade, Enforcer, Sleepwalker-style random visits. If one of them fits, the argument is weak. A teammate pushing this line hard is a Yakuza signal.

Two investigators checking the same target on Night 1 is a split, not a contradiction. Don't spend days on it. Ask for the second night's target and exact result in the same message, and nominate on whichever contradiction comes back first, rather than on silence from the suspect.

lessons.applies_to: Jester or any Neutral seeking a hanging
lessons.tip: A bare self-nomination with no data gets only one Yes and fails. To get hanged, you need a visible lead that a majority wants to act on, such as pointing at a claim with a checkable contradiction. Prepare that case before Day 2 instead of relying on a test nomination.

Protect the Veteran or Tracker claim that your Katana can expose. Carol was killed as a Tracker, and the Veteran's remaining claim was then argued against by the Yakuza's own 'visit logic' framing. Pushing 'publicly fake visit logic' against a real Village claimant has to be coordinated with the Pharmacist's and Grunt's stories, or it reads as a targeted vote.

tips_feedback.tip: A self-nomination or push without data while reading Evil is often a Jester: prefer leaving them alive, or hang with a bare Guilty majority.
tips_feedback.why: As Jester this predicted my own test nomination, and Alice cited it to keep me alive. The town simply declined to hang me, so the self-nomination was wasted and the tip made my win harder.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. A lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof only when corroborated; one unverified log is just a claim.
tips_feedback.why: The town and Bob used this to attack Alice's Veteran claim as a lie. The visitor was explained by Grace's hidden Sleepwalker visit, so the tip was followed in a way that misled the vote onto a real Village claimant.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post important results while alive.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's will recorded her Night 1 Tracker result and her Night 2 target, so her information reached the town after her death.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; held-back results tend to look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Carol delayed their Night 2 results to Day 3, which made the town treat them as suspicious and pushed the vote toward the Yakuza-aligned argument.

You were also given tips from past games (in your instructions). Which of them went especially well or badly for you or others this game? List only tips that clearly mattered (or none): helped, hurt (followed it and it backfired, or it was predictable to opponents), or wrong (it is false or contradicts the rules), and why, concretely.

lessons.tip: When a town member asks a direct yes/no about your Katana or holder status, give a flat answer, even a lie. Repeated non-answers ('no claim, I won't vote on claims') read as guilt and became the lynch case, with 5 Guilty votes. A plain denial is cheaper than silence.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza with Sleepwalker or other random-visit traits
lessons.tip: A random Sleepwalker visit can land on a Veteran on alert and kill you, and it can also create visits you can't explain. Before attacking or blocking on a night you have a random visit, consider that the random target may be an alert Veteran, and count that risk in the plan.

Don't use daytime private messages between teammates. Two Day PMs (Bob to Grace, then Bob to Frank and Heidi) were noticed at once and became the trial's main lead. Keep all coordination in night chat, as the older tip says.

When a claim needs a visit the public record doesn't show (for example a Veteran kill by a visitor who visited nobody else publicly), first ask whether a hidden random-visit trait such as Sleepwalker explains it. Ask the claimant or the suspected teammate directly before voting on the visit logic alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Announced actors are usually that night's kill or block (Village/Yakuza night targeting).
tips_feedback.why: Carol claimed Tracker on Day 2 and was killed by the Katana that night; Erin claimed Sheriff on Day 2 and was blocked by my Pharmacist. Targeting the claimed investigators was the right call and matched what the tip predicted.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep plans in night chat; daytime PMs between teammates are visible to all and often become the town's main lead.
tips_feedback.why: This was a warning Bob ignored. Carol flagged the Day 1 PM, and the Day 3 PMs to Frank and Heidi became the trial's central topic, which hurt the Yakuza side. Bob's behaviour bore out the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: Confirm holder and target nightly and submit every Katana vote.
tips_feedback.why: Both Katana votes on Night 1 and Night 2 were submitted and matched, so the Night 2 Katana attack on Carol went through as planned.

output.reason: Game is over; I'm giving post-game lessons and tip feedback only, so the other fields are left empty.

reasoning:
I need to produce a structured output with lessons and tips_feedback since the game has ended with a Village win. Reflecting as Grace, the dead Yakuza Pharmacist, the key lesson is that Bob's Night 1 decision not to kill and his refusal to answer the Katana question proved fatal for the Yakuza, since that non-answer tipped the town off.

Alice's Veteran claim turned out to be accurate—Grace's own Sleepwalker trait had caused her to visit Alice, something Bob didn't realize when he pushed back on that claim. Meanwhile Grace's Pharmacist block on Erin successfully disrupted Erin's Sheriff action on Night 2, and the Yakuza's passivity on Night 1 followed by killing Carol on Night 2 wasn't enough to overcome the town's momentum once Bob's Day 3 defense started faltering.

Bob's refusal to answer the direct Katana question looked worse than a flat denial would have, which taught me Sleepwalker's random visits are a double-edged sword—great cover, but risky for a Yakuza since they can accidentally trigger a Veteran's alert. Also worth noting: Bob's daytime PMs to Grace were visible and became a key piece of evidence against them, violating the night-chat-only guidance, and his lone Innocent vote on a doomed teammate only made things look worse.

The tip about convicting on corroborated mechanical claims held up well, since Alice's investigation result was accurate and the town largely trusted it; counting vote locks also mattered, as Erin's Day 3 nomination against Bob gathered enough support to proceed. I'm now going through which tips clearly "helped" versus "hurt" — the daytime-PM warning seems to have been accurate as a prediction (since Bob's PMs became the central lead against him) even though Bob himself ignored it.

Working through the remaining tips: confirming the Katana holder nightly and submitting votes correctly helped the Yakuza land their kill on Night 2, while the advice against hinting at power roles early proved true, since both Carol and Erin claimed roles on Day 2 and were immediately targeted — Carol killed, Erin blocked. Other tips about defending doomed teammates or post-failed-Katana assumptions weren't really applicable here.

I'm drafting the lessons now: one on how Bob's non-answers about his Katana status became costly compared to a flat denial, one on how Grace's random Sleepwalker-type visit got her killed by an alert Veteran and also validated Alice's claim, one on avoiding daytime PMs between teammates since both got used as trial evidence, and one for the Village side about considering hidden random-visit traits before judging claims. I'll leave other categories like confusing rules or bugs empty since there's nothing meaningful there, and finalize three tips_feedback entries matching the lessons above.

Pushing 'publicly fake visit logic' against a real Village claimant has to be coordinated with the Pharmacist's and Grunt's stories, or it reads as a targeted vote.

tips_feedback.tip: A self-nomination or push without data while reading Evil is often a Jester: prefer leaving them alive, or hang with a bare Guilty majority.
tips_feedback.why: As Jester this predicted my own test nomination, and Alice cited it to keep me alive. The town simply declined to hang me, so the self-nomination was wasted and the tip made my win harder.

tips_feedback.tip: A visit shows a destination, not an action. A lone unexplained visitor to a Katana victim is near-proof only when corroborated; one unverified log is just a claim.
tips_feedback.why: The town and Bob used this to attack Alice's Veteran claim as a lie. The visitor was explained by Grace's hidden Sleepwalker visit, so the tip was followed in a way that misled the vote onto a real Village claimant.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep past results and tonight's plan in your will; the result of the night you die never reaches it, so post important results while alive.
tips_feedback.why: Carol's will recorded her Night 1 Tracker result and her Night 2 target, so her information reached the town after her death.

tips_feedback.tip: Investigators: post night, target and exact result once it bears on a vote; held-back results tend to look retrofitted.
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Carol delayed their Night 2 results to Day 3, which made the town treat them as suspicious and pushed the vote toward the Yakuza-aligned argument.

lessons.tip: When a town member asks a direct yes/no about your Katana or holder status, give a flat answer, even a lie. Repeated non-answers ('no claim, I won't vote on claims') read as guilt and became the lynch case, with 5 Guilty votes. A plain denial is cheaper than silence.

lessons.applies_to: Yakuza with Sleepwalker or other random-visit traits
lessons.tip: A random Sleepwalker visit can land on a Veteran on alert and kill you, and it can also create visits you can't explain. Before attacking or blocking on a night you have a random visit, consider that the random target may be an alert Veteran, and count that risk in the plan.

Don't use daytime private messages between teammates. Two Day PMs (Bob to Grace, then Bob to Frank and Heidi) were noticed at once and became the trial's main lead. Keep all coordination in night chat, as the older tip says.

When a claim needs a visit the public record doesn't show (for example a Veteran kill by a visitor who visited nobody else publicly), first ask whether a hidden random-visit trait such as Sleepwalker explains it. Ask the claimant or the suspected teammate directly before voting on the visit logic alone.

tips_feedback.tip: Announced actors are usually that night's kill or block (Village/Yakuza night targeting).
tips_feedback.why: Carol claimed Tracker on Day 2 and was killed by the Katana that night; Erin claimed Sheriff on Day 2 and was blocked by my Pharmacist. Targeting the claimed investigators was the right call and matched what the tip predicted.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep plans in night chat; daytime PMs between teammates are visible to all and often become the town's main lead.
tips_feedback.why: This was a warning Bob ignored. Carol flagged the Day 1 PM, and the Day 3 PMs to Frank and Heidi became the trial's central topic, which hurt the Yakuza side. Bob's behaviour bore out the tip.

tips_feedback.tip: Confirm holder and target nightly and submit every Katana vote.
tips_feedback.why: Both Katana votes on Night 1 and Night 2 were submitted and matched, so the Night 2 Katana attack on Carol went through as planned.

lessons.tip: Hidden traits can add visits nobody can see. Alice's Veteran claim looked impossible from public visits, but Grace had a Sleepwalker trait that visited a random player each night. Before doubting a visit-based claim, ask whether a hidden Sleepwalker, Armed or similar trait could explain the extra visit, and don't let a Yakuza's 'the visits don't fit' argument decide your vote for you.

A Not Evil result on a player who may hold the Katana proves nothing, because the holder reads Good that night. Treat a Sheriff's Not Evil on a suspect as weak until you know whether that suspect was the Katana holder. Yakuza-holder checks matter more when they are repeated over several nights.

When a player repeatedly refuses a direct yes/no question (here, 'did you hold the Katana?') while pushing the table toward other people's claims, count that as a real signal. Ask once with a clear deadline and then vote on it, rather than accepting non-answers for three days.

Post your results early and exactly, with target and outcome. A Tracker who checks a Yakuza holder and then dies to the Katana gives the town a strong clue, but only if that result is public before the death; holding results back let the Yakuza frame the discussion around 'who claims what'.

On Days 2-3 the town spent a full day repeating 'no nomination, post your results' without making progress. Agree on a concrete vote trigger early, such as a named suspect plus a named test, so that the Yakuza don't get free days to sow doubt about the true Veteran.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the rules before calling a contradiction: a block or swap can explain a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: Bob used this exact line to argue Alice's Veteran claim didn't fit the visits. The real explanation was a Sleepwalker trait the town couldn't see, so the tip made me hesitate over the true Veteran's account instead of looking for hidden-trait explanations.

tips_feedback.tip: Someone who self-nominates or pushes without data while reading Evil is often a Jester: prefer leaving them alive.
tips_feedback.why: Frank's self-nomination looked like bait and I voted No. Frank was the Jester, and the town didn't hang him on bare behaviour, which kept a Jester win from being handed over.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep plans in night chat; daytime PMs between teammates are visible to all and often become the town's main lead.
tips_feedback.why: Bob's repeated PMs to Grace (Days 1-2) and to Frank and Heidi (Day 3) were visible to everyone and became a major line of suspicion against him, which fed into his trial.

summary: The Village won on Day 3 by hanging the last Yakuza, Bob. The Yakuza lost mostly through their own visible play. On Day 1, Bob sent Grace a private message that everyone could see had been sent. That made them the only standout players, so on Night 1 three investigators targeted them: Carol tracked Bob, Erin checked Bob as Sheriff, and Dave watched Grace as Lookout. The Yakuza then skipped their Night 1 kill, which gave the Village a free round of checks. On Day 2, Bob was asked about eight times whether he had held the Katana (the Yakuza weapon, whose holder reads Not Evil to a Sheriff). He never gave a yes or no, and that refusal became the whole case against him. Frank, the Jester, nominated himself with no data. The town saw it as bait (Alice named it a likely Jester play), and the nomination got only Frank's own Yes vote. On Night 2 the Yakuza made two good moves: they killed Carol, the claimed Tracker, and Grace's Pharmacist block hit Erin, who was checking Grace that night. But Grace's Sleepwalker trait sent her on a random visit to Alice, a Veteran on alert, and the counterattack killed her. That left Bob alone. Dave's Lookout result (Carol and Grace visited Erin) matched Erin being role-blocked and Carol's Tracker claim. Erin then nominated Bob for his evasions. Bob's defense rested on the false idea that Grace could not have visited both Erin and Alice, which a Sleepwalker visit easily explains. He was hanged 5-1. Village mistakes: Carol publicly claimed Tracker on Day 2 and was killed that night. No one spelled out the strongest mechanical read: Erin was blocked and only Carol and Grace visited her, so Grace was the blocker and likely Yakuza.

lessons.tip: Plan an answer to the obvious yes/no questions (such as 'Did you hold the Katana?') before Day 2. Then answer briefly and consistently. Dodging the same direct question for a whole Day becomes the case against you, even if no result says you are Evil.
lessons.evidence: Bob was asked about eight times on Day 2 whether he held the Katana and replied each time with 'no claim, I want data.' On Day 3, Erin nominated him because of that refusal, and Alice, Dave, Erin and Heidi all named it in their Guilty reasoning.

lessons.tip: Never send daytime private messages to a teammate. Everyone can see that a message was sent, and on early days it is often the only event, so it decides who the investigators check that night. Keep all plans for night chat.
lessons.evidence: Bob sent Grace a private message on Day 1, and Carol pointed it out publicly. That night Carol tracked Bob, Erin checked Bob and Dave watched Grace. On Day 3, Heidi and Alice asked Bob to explain the private messages.

lessons.tip: Don't skip the Night 1 kill in a small game. Each night without a kill gives every investigator a free result and takes nothing from the Village. Kill a vocal player or the person driving suspicion toward your team.
lessons.evidence: The Yakuza agreed on 'no kill, no block' on Night 1. Carol, who had pressed Bob and Grace on Day 1, survived to claim Tracker. All three investigators got a free look at the Yakuza pair.

lessons.tip: Combine a block report with the Lookout's list of visitors. If a player says they were role-blocked and the Lookout saw only one visitor whose action is unexplained, that visitor is very likely the blocker. A blocker is most often the Yakuza Pharmacist, so their daytime private-message partner becomes the top suspect.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2, Erin was role-blocked and Dave saw only Carol (claimed Tracker) and Grace visit her. So Grace was the blocker, which tied Bob to the Yakuza through his private messages to her. No one stated this chain. Bob was hanged on behavior alone.

lessons.tip: A player can visit more than one person in a night: their own action plus a Sleepwalker visit or a Katana attack. Before calling a claim impossible because 'X only visited Y,' check whether a second visit could explain it.
lessons.evidence: In his trial, Bob argued that Alice's Veteran kill of Grace contradicted Dave's report that Grace visited Erin. Dave, Erin and Heidi answered that a second visit, for example from a Sleepwalker, explains it, and this was in fact what happened. His defense collapsed and the vote was 5-1.

lessons.tip: Use alerts on the early nights, before you claim, when visits are spread around randomly. After an alert kill, claim Veteran the next Day so the town reads the dead visitor correctly.
lessons.evidence: Alice alerted on Nights 1 and 2 without claiming. Grace's Sleepwalker visit ran into the Night 2 alert, killing one of the two Yakuza. Alice claimed right away on Day 3, which explained the death and kept the town's attention on Bob.

lessons.tip: A self-nomination with no data is the most recognizable Jester move, and it almost never gets a majority. Instead, create mild suspicion through small factual errors or odd votes that make you look like a Yakuza, and push for a nomination only when the town is short of leads.
lessons.evidence: Frank nominated himself on Day 2 and got only his own Yes vote. Alice publicly called it 'bait, possibly a Jester play,' and the town stopped considering him.

lessons.tip: Hold back a power-role claim until your result can actually decide a vote. A Day 2 claim of a result that decides nothing mostly makes you the night's kill target.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2, Carol claimed Tracker with an inconclusive result about Bob, and the Yakuza killed her that night because she was 'the bigger threat.' Erin also claimed (Sheriff) and was the target of Grace's block.

tips_feedback.tip: Keep plans in night chat; daytime PMs between teammates are visible to all and often become the town's main lead.
tips_feedback.why: The tip proved accurate. Bob ignored it by messaging Grace on Days 1 and 2. Those messages decided all three Night 1 investigations and were cited against Bob at his trial.

tips_feedback.tip: The Katana holder reads Not Evil, so a clean read clears no one outright; an Evil read also fits a Jester, Executioner, Ex-Con or frame.
tips_feedback.why: Erin, Grace, Heidi and Alice all said that Erin's Not Evil result on Bob fit the Katana-holder exception. Bob was never treated as cleared, which kept the question 'Did you hold the Katana?' alive until he was hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Someone who self-nominates or pushes without data while reading Evil is often a Jester: prefer leaving them alive, or hang with a bare Guilty majority.
tips_feedback.why: Alice called Frank's self-nomination likely Jester bait. Frank was in fact the Jester, the nomination got 1 Yes vote, and the Jester never had a path to win.

tips_feedback.tip: Check the rules before calling a contradiction: only Smuggler and Vulture are Unique, so duplicate claimants are often both real, and a block or swap can explain a missing or odd result.
tips_feedback.why: Carol, Dave and Erin corrected Frank's claim that the Sheriff and Tracker results contradicted each other. On Day 3, villagers rejected Bob's claim that the visits made Alice's account impossible by pointing to possible extra visits.

tips_feedback.tip: Avoid hinting at a power role on Day 1-2 or announcing tonight's target, even by PM (a Wiretap may read it): announced actors are usually that night's kill or block.
tips_feedback.why: Events proved it right. Carol and Erin claimed on Day 2, and that night Carol was killed and Erin was blocked, exactly as the tip warns.

tips_feedback.tip: Convict on corroborated mechanical cases (a broken claim, an attack slip, a lone unexplained visitor) rather than wording or leans; when no result is coming, hang the best lead available.
tips_feedback.why: On Day 3, with their best lead identified and Erin's result blocked, the town hanged Bob rather than waiting another night. That won the game.

tips_feedback.tip: Count the vote lock each morning: Yakuza holding half the living block every nomination, so 'wait for tonight's results' usually just costs an investigator.
tips_feedback.why: Events proved it right. The whole town chose to wait on Day 2 despite Bob's evasions, and Carol was killed that night. The game still went the Village's way only because of Grace's lucky Veteran death.

issues.description: Night 2: Grace (Pharmacist) received a private moderator message 'You visited Erin tonight.' R9 says a role-blocker learns only whether the block failed because the target can't be role-blocked. This extra confirmation isn't in the rules. It leaked nothing hidden because she chose the target herself, but it is output the rules don't provide for and could read as a result.

Frank's in-game feedback said the action schema requires many fields even when unused, and that the nominate/target fields are typed as nullable strings, which made formatting awkward until he used plain values. This interface friction could cause malformed or mistaken actions.

Day 2: Frank claimed 'Erin and Carol cannot both be right about a single Bob check without someone lying.' A Sheriff's Not Evil and a Tracker's no-visit result are independent and fully compatible (and both were true). Three players corrected him. As the Jester he may have said it deliberately as bait, but the statement misreads the mechanics.
